title: DCAF11-dependent molecular glue degrader activated by glutathionylation.
data_url: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/archive/projects/PXD067076 (plus PXD067016, PXD067063, PXD067066, PXD067067, PXD067070; code at https://github.com/Yoonlab-MDA/DCAF11_Nature2026)

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed every file in all six PRIDE (PRoteomics IDEntifications archive) depositions via the PRIDE API: 163 files, almost all raw mass-spectrometry data (.raw, .d.zip up to 1.7 GB each) plus a few processed tables. Downloaded and parsed the smallest processed table (ip-esf_549...pr_matrix_edit.tsv, 4.9 MB): it is a DIA-NN precursor-intensity matrix with 27,188 peptide-precursor rows, 3,804 protein groups and only 8 mass-spectrometry runs as columns, 21-30% missing values per run, no treatment/compound annotation and no outcome column. Also listed the GitHub repository: 5 R scripts, no data files.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The screen design (7 E3 ubiquitin ligases x 5,000 compounds from the MedChemExpress '5K Scaffold Library' HY-L902, pooled 320 compounds per pool, read out by immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry), the identification of M12 as a DCAF11 glue degrading DDX18, the CRISPR screens, and the cryo-EM structure (PDB 9PTU). Europe PMC's supplementary-file listing timed out twice, so the 'Source data for main figures' file was not retrievable.

a1_downloadable.note: PRIDE depositions are public and open; I downloaded a 4.9 MB processed matrix with no login. Most files are raw mass spectrometry (0.8-1.7 GB each), which this project does not download.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. No outcome column anywhere. The compound-level label (does this molecule glue a protein to an E3 ligase?) does not exist at all because 5,000 compounds were screened in pools of 320 with a single pooled readout, and only one hit (M12) was deconvoluted. A protein-level 'degraded / not degraded' label would have to be constructed by running differential-abundance analysis on raw precursor intensities with sample-to-condition mapping that is not in the deposited files.

a3_inputs_present.note: Protein inputs are present as UniProt accessions and gene symbols in the matrix; compound structures are not deposited but the library is a named commercial catalogue (MedChemExpress HY-L902), so structures are obtainable.

a4_units_stated.note: Columns are DIA-NN precursor intensities (arbitrary units, documented by the DIA-NN format); the paper states compound concentrations (1 uM in pools, 10 uM M12).

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL for every task on offer. The deposited processed matrix I opened has 8 mass-spectrometry runs; the other has 6. The experimental unit for a glue-activity model is the compound-pool (about 16 pools x 7 ligases) or the single deconvoluted compound M12, and for a degradability model it is the handful of proteins shown to be degraded. 27,188 precursor rows are repeated measurements of 3,804 proteins across 8 runs, not 27,188 labelled examples.

a6_fits_laptop.note: The processed tables are tiny and parse in seconds on a laptop; the raw .d.zip folders (about 15 GB total) would not be needed and are excluded by policy.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to contradict: the paper gives no row counts for a feature table, and the file I opened matches its own header (8 run columns for 8 deposited .d.zip files in that deposition).

a8_label_provenance.note: Where a quantity exists it is a real physical measurement (mass-spectrometry peptide intensity), not another model's output. The problem is that no label is defined, not that the label is circular.

existing_models.name: DeepPROTACs (Nature Communications 2022), deep neural network predicting degradation from target protein and E3 ligase structures plus the PROTAC molecule
existing_models.score_and_split: Authors report 77.95% average accuracy and 0.847 area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve on their test set; split is effectively random over PROTAC-DB entries, so it is an optimistic estimate.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalisation to unseen target proteins and new E3 ligases beyond the handful (cereblon, VHL) that dominate the training data.

existing_models.name: SE(3)-PROTACs (Briefings in Bioinformatics 2026), geometry-aware transformer with ESM (Evolutionary Scale Modeling) protein-language-model embeddings
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported on the PROTAC-DB-derived benchmark of roughly 2,000 curated PROTAC samples; exact split not verified by me beyond the abstract.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Small labelled datasets and the scarcity of ternary-complex structures.

existing_models.name: Pocket-PROTACs (2026), pocket-aware attention model over target protein, E3 ligase and compound conformers
existing_models.score_and_split: Evaluated on PROTAC-8K, described as the largest public labelled degradability dataset, curated from PROTAC-DB 3.0; split details not verified.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Which protein surfaces are degradable at all, and transfer to molecular glues rather than bivalent PROTACs.

existing_models.name: MolGlueDB (2025) plus the literature-curated molecular-glue classifiers built on it (2,091 glues versus 196 non-glues)
existing_models.score_and_split: Database of 1,840 entries, 1,629 distinct glue degraders, 28 recruiting proteins, 94 targets; the paired classifiers report cross-validated accuracy on a strongly imbalanced literature set.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Almost no true negatives, and coverage limited to cereblon and a few other ligases.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (protein language model) for substrate sequences plus ChemBERTa for compounds would be the obvious pair
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would suffice for the few thousand proteins involved
backbone.licence: Both permissive (MIT-style), but irrelevant here because no labels exist to fit a head to

integration.partner_dataset: MolGlueDB / PROTAC-DB 3.0 for compound-level degradation labels, and DepMap or the Human Protein Atlas for substrate-level context
integration.join_key: UniProt accession for proteins, InChIKey for compounds
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which protein surfaces can be made degradable by a glue acting through a non-cereblon E3 ligase? - a real question, but this paper contributes one compound and one substrate to it, not a dataset.

controls.positive_control: DDX18 depletion on M12 treatment, which the authors demonstrate - but a single known positive is a sanity check, not a control set
controls.negative_control: DMSO (vehicle) runs are present in the depositions, though the run-to-condition mapping is not in the deposited tables
controls.external_validation: MolGlueDB and PROTAC-DB hold independent degradation data, but they cover cereblon-centric chemistry and do not contain DCAF11 glues

honest_claim_h3: No honest model-level claim is available: the deposited data support the statement 'M12 degrades DDX18 and several other proteins through DCAF11', which is the paper's own biology, and nothing a model could be trained on or tested against.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a small molecule's chemical structure to predict whether it glues a target protein to a specific protein-destroying enzyme.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on each compound's chemical structure paired with each E3 ubiquitin ligase (the enzyme that tags proteins for destruction), labelled by whether a protein was pulled down and degraded. In this paper that would be 5,000 compounds x 7 ligases, but the measurements were pooled 320 compounds at a time, so the real number of labelled examples is about 112 pools, of which one was broken down to a single compound.
plain_idea.predict: Output would be a degradation call or fold-change per compound-protein pair. The truth comes from immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry: ligases are incubated with cell extract and compounds, and protein abundance is measured on a mass spectrometer.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups designing molecular glue degraders (for example the Ebert and Fischer labs at Dana-Farber, and most targeted-protein-degradation companies) badly need data on non-cereblon ligases, because almost all public glue data is cereblon-centric. Even a failed model would map which protein surfaces are reachable.

more_or_better_data.why: The deposited processed data are two precursor-intensity matrices covering 8 and 6 mass-spectrometry runs. MolGlueDB alone holds 1,629 distinct glue degraders and PROTAC-DB-derived PROTAC-8K about 2,000 labelled samples; this paper adds one compound.

confidence_score.why: There are replicate runs (DMSO versus M12, n=4 per the figure legends), which would let you estimate measurement noise for a protein, but with a single compound there is nothing to give per-prediction confidence about.

models_beatable.why: DeepPROTACs (2022) reports 0.847 area under the ROC curve on an effectively random split of PROTAC-DB and is beatable in principle; but beating it needs the PROTAC-DB/MolGlueDB data, not this paper, so this paper gives no edge.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails on the first condition: this paper provides no labelled examples that could be added to an existing model's training set, so there is nothing to join and no shared split.

ml_idea: The tempting idea - learn molecular-glue activity from the structures of 5,000 screened compounds across 7 E3 ligases - cannot be built from this paper because the screen was read out in pools of 320 compounds and only one hit was resolved to a single molecule. The fallback idea, predicting which proteins a DCAF11 glue can degrade from protein sequence, has a handful of positives. Both die on example count, not on data access.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the one file I actually parsed: a 4.9 MB tab-separated matrix loaded into pandas in a few seconds with well under 1 GB of memory. No cross-validation or embedding estimate is meaningful because there is no labelled set.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the number of distinct compound-level labels in the deposited files. I did this: zero. The library was screened in pools of 320 and only M12 was deconvoluted, so a compound-to-activity table does not exist.

verdict_reason: A2 and A5 fail on the files, not just on the paper. This is a mechanism-of-action study whose public data are raw and lightly processed mass-spectrometry runs (the processed matrix I opened has 8 runs, 3,804 proteins, 21-30% missing values, no condition or compound annotation and no outcome column). The 5,000-compound screen that makes the paper sound dataset-like was read out in pools of 320 compounds, so no per-compound label was ever measured, and only one compound (M12) was resolved. Building either candidate label - compound glue activity, or protein degradability - would mean constructing the target from scratch, and the result would have single-digit positives. The underlying question is a good one, but the data for it lives in MolGlueDB and PROTAC-DB, not here.
